newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia grain area halved, limited losses in north.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia grain area halved, limited losses in north.

text.p: Tunisia's cereals area for the new season has been cut by half compared with last year because of low rainfall in central and southern areas, Agriculture Minister Mabrouk Bahri said on Thursday.
"Most of the southern and central areas were not sown," he told a news briefing.
"Total areas sown were one million hectares, mostly in the northern region with 784,000 hectares," he said.
Traders said the cut in the area sown would not mean an equivalent sharp drop in the grain output.
"The northern region remains Tunisia's main grain provider, and so far rains were good there. The central and southern regions' input had always been relatively marginal," one trader said.
Area sown last season totalled two million hectares, including 1.1 million in the southern and central regions, revised official data showed.
Cereals output reached a record 2.867 million tonnes.
"The crop's situation is normal as to now," Mabrouk said, expressing hopes that more rains would fall during the next few weeks.
He said that the country's dams were at 83 percent of their capacity.
Drought cut the 1995 harvest to 0.62 million tonnes and the 1994 harvest to 0.65 million, from a 1993 crop of 1.91 million tonnes.
Domestic consuption was estimated at 2.2 million tonnes in 1995.
